title: Hello, Mandarin
description: Start a friendly conversation and say goodbye.

dialogue.speaker: Lin
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ hěn hǎo, xièxie. Nǐ ne?

note.title: Two third tones together
note.body: In 你好 (nǐ hǎo), the first third tone is pronounced like a rising second tone because another third tone follows. We keep the dictionary tone marks for third tones throughout the lessons. The second syllable of 谢谢 (xièxie) is light and unmarked: a neutral tone.

title: What’s your name?
description: Introduce yourself and ask someone’s name.

dialogue.speaker: Lin
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo! Wǒ jiào Lín Ān.
dialogue.english: Hello! My name is Lin An.

dialogue.speaker: Lin
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ jiào wǒ Xiǎo Lín.
dialogue.english: You can call me Xiao Lin.

note.title: Ask with 什么
note.body: 你叫什么名字？ means “What’s your name?” The question word 什么 stays where the answer would go: 我叫林安。 Don’t add 吗 to a question that already uses a question word.

title: Meet the four tones
description: Hear how pitch changes a syllable’s meaning.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.pinyin: Qǐng tīng: mā, má, mǎ, mà.
dialogue.english: Please listen: mother, hemp, horse, scold.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.pinyin: Duì. Qǐng zài shuō yí biàn.

note.title: Listen for the four tones
note.body: The marks show four tones: mā stays high, má rises, mǎ dips and rises when spoken alone, and mà falls sharply. In connected speech, a third tone often stays low without rising. Unmarked syllables have a short, light neutral tone. Within phrases, our pinyin shows the spoken tone changes of 一 and 不.

title: A little more slowly
description: Ask for a slower pace when you practise listening.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.english: Did you understand what you heard?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: Please speak a little more slowly.

note.title: Make a polite request
note.body: Put 请 before the action: 请听 means “Please listen.” 慢一点 means “a little more slowly.” In 不客气, 不 changes from bù to bú before the fourth tone in 客 (kè). This change is shown in the pinyin.

title: Count to ten
description: Build numbers and count things around you.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.pinyin: Qǐng cóng yī shǔ dào shí.
dialogue.english: Please count from one to ten.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.pinyin: Hěn hǎo! Zhèlǐ yǒu jǐ ge bēizi?
dialogue.english: Very good! How many cups are here?

note.title: Numbers and measure words
note.body: To count many everyday objects, use a number + 个 + noun: 三个杯子 means “three cups.” 个 is a common measure word, but other nouns use different ones. 一 is yī when counting. Eleven is 十一 (shíyī); twenty is 二十 (èrshí).

title: What’s the date?
description: Talk about today, tomorrow, and birthdays.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ de shēngrì shì jiǔ yuè qī hào?

note.title: Month before day
note.body: Say the month before the day: 九月七号 is September seventh. Months use a number + 月, so 一月 is January and 十二月 is December. 号 is common when saying dates. The dates in this dialogue are examples.

title: Where are you from?
description: Say where you’re from and what you’re learning.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ shì Yuènán rén. Nǐ ne?

note.title: Introduce with 是
note.body: The pattern person + 是 + identity says who someone is: 我是越南人。 Add 人 after a country’s name to describe a person from that country. In 我在学中文, 在 before the verb marks an ongoing action.

title: What is this?
description: Name things nearby and ask about things farther away.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Zhè shì nǐ de bǐ ma?

note.title: Show possession with 的
note.body: Put 的 between the person and the object: 我的手机 means “my phone”; 你的笔 means “your pen.” Add 吗 at the end to make a yes-or-no question: 这是你的笔吗？

title: My family
description: Introduce family members and say how many people live at home.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén?
dialogue.english: How many people are in your family?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén.
dialogue.english: There are four people in my family.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.pinyin: Tā yě zhù zài zhèlǐ ma?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.hanzi: 不，她和爸爸妈妈住在一起。
dialogue.pinyin: Bù, tā hé bàba māma zhù zài yìqǐ.
dialogue.english: No, she lives with our parents.

note.title: Count family members with 口
note.body: When counting people in a household, use 口: 四口人 means “four people.” 有 means “to have” or “there is.” To say you don’t have something, use 没有 (méiyǒu), as in 我没有姐姐: “I don’t have an older sister.”

title: Work and study
description: Ask about work and describe a student’s routine.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: What do you do for work?

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.english: Do you have classes every day?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.hanzi: 我星期一到星期五上课。
dialogue.english: I have classes from Monday to Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.english: You can rest on the weekend.

vocabulary.english: to attend or teach a class

note.title: Days of the week
note.body: Monday through Saturday use 星期 + a number: 星期一 is Monday and 星期五 is Friday. Sunday is 星期天 or 星期日. Put time before the action: 我星期一上课 means “I have class on Monday.”

title: What time is it?
description: Read the clock and work out when class starts.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: What time does our class start?

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān hē bēi chá ba.
dialogue.english: Let’s have a cup of tea first.

note.title: Clock time and duration
note.body: Use 点 for clock time: 八点 is eight o’clock, and 八点半 is eight thirty. Use 小时 for a duration: 半个小时 is half an hour. “Two o’clock” is 两点 (liǎng diǎn), while “two hours” is 两个小时.

title: Things you enjoy
description: Share your interests and find something you both enjoy.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.hanzi: 我喜欢听音乐，也喜欢看书。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan tīng yīnyuè, yě xǐhuan kàn shū.
dialogue.english: I like listening to music and reading.

note.title: Say what you like doing
note.body: Put the activity right after 喜欢: 我喜欢听音乐 means “I like listening to music.” 也 goes before the verb or verb phrase: 我也喜欢跑步。 Use 吧 at the end to make a friendly suggestion.

title: Where is my phone?
description: Find everyday objects with simple location words.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.hanzi: 不在。桌子上只有一本书。
dialogue.pinyin: Bú zài. Zhuōzi shàng zhǐ yǒu yì běn shū.
dialogue.english: No. There’s only a book on the table.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: Found it! It’s in the bag.

note.title: Put the location after 在
note.body: Use object + 在 + place: 手机在包里 means “The phone is in the bag.” Location words follow the noun, so 桌子上 means “on the table.” To ask where, replace the place with 哪里: 手机在哪里？

title: How much is it?
description: Ask the price and buy some fruit.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, píngguǒ duōshao qián yì jīn?
dialogue.english: Excuse me, how much are the apples per jin?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: Can I pay by scanning a QR code?

note.title: Two: 二 or 两?
note.body: Use 两 before most measure words: 两斤 means two jin. In mainland China, one 斤 is 500 grams, so 两斤 is one kilogram. Use 二 inside numbers such as 十二 (twelve) and 二十 (twenty). 块 is an everyday way to say yuan.

title: Let’s order lunch
description: Order a simple meal and explain your preferences.

dialogue.speaker: Server
dialogue.english: What would you like to eat?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: I’d like a bowl of noodles.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.hanzi: 我要一碗米饭和一份炒青菜。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ yào yì wǎn mǐfàn hé yí fèn chǎo qīngcài.
dialogue.english: I’d like a bowl of rice and a portion of stir-fried greens.

dialogue.speaker: Server
dialogue.english: Would you like the noodles spicy?

vocabulary.english: bowl; measure word for a bowlful

note.title: Order with 我要
note.body: 我要 + food is a common way to order: 我要一碗面条。 Use 碗 for a bowlful and 份 for a serving. 一 changes tone before another syllable: yì before third-tone 碗, but yí before fourth-tone 份.

title: Tea or coffee?
description: Choose a drink, ask for less sugar, and take it away.

dialogue.speaker: Server
dialogue.english: What would you like to drink?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yào yì bēi lǜchá.
dialogue.english: I’d like a cup of green tea.

dialogue.speaker: Server
dialogue.english: For here or to take away?

note.title: Offer a choice with 还是
note.body: Use A + 还是 + B to ask someone to choose: 热的还是冰的？ means “Hot or iced?” 的 lets an adjective stand in for the drink. In 绿 (lǜ), keep your tongue as if saying “ee” and round your lips to make ü.

title: Finding your way
description: Ask for directions and follow a short route.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: Excuse me, how do I get to the subway station?

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.hanzi: 到路口右转。地铁站在左边。
dialogue.pinyin: Dào lùkǒu yòu zhuǎn. Dìtiězhàn zài zuǒbian.
dialogue.english: Turn right at the intersection. The subway station is on the left.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: How long does it take to walk there?

note.title: Put directions in order
note.body: 先 means “first,” and 然后 means “then.” 往 marks a direction: 往前走 means “walk forward.” To ask how long an action takes, use 要多久: 走路要多久？

title: Take the subway
description: Find the right line and check where to get off.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Qù huǒchēzhàn zuò jǐ hào xiàn?
dialogue.english: Which subway line goes to the train station?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: Do I need to change trains?

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.pinyin: Bú yòng, zuò sān zhàn jiù dào le.
dialogue.english: No, it’s just three stops away.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ zài huǒchēzhàn xià chē, duì ma?
dialogue.english: I get off at the train station, right?

note.title: Use 坐 for transport
note.body: 坐 can mean “to take” a form of transport: 坐地铁 means “take the subway.” With numbered lines, use 二: 二号线 is Line 2. 不用 means “there’s no need”; 别 + action tells someone not to do it. This route is a practice example.

title: A typical day
description: Describe your morning and when you head to work.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.english: What time do you get up every day?

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.english: What do you do after getting up?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Xiān xǐ liǎn, ránhòu chī zǎofàn.
dialogue.english: First I wash my face, then I have breakfast.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.english: What time do you leave home?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.hanzi: 八点出门，坐公交车去上班。
dialogue.pinyin: Bā diǎn chūmén, zuò gōngjiāochē qù shàngbān.
dialogue.english: I leave at eight and take the bus to work.

vocabulary.english: to go out; to leave home

note.title: Say what happens afterward
note.body: Put 以后 after an action to mean “after doing it”: 起床以后 means “after getting up.” A useful pattern is time + action: 七点起床，八点出门。 Mandarin verbs do not change their form for different subjects.

title: What’s the weather like?
description: Talk about rain and make a plan for the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒudiǎn lěng, hái zài xià yǔ.
dialogue.english: It’s a little cold, and it’s still raining.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Xiàwǔ yě huì xià yǔ ma?
dialogue.english: Will it rain in the afternoon too?

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.hanzi: 天气预报说下午有太阳。
dialogue.pinyin: Tiānqì yùbào shuō xiàwǔ yǒu tàiyáng.
dialogue.english: The forecast says it’ll be sunny in the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: Then let’s go out in the afternoon.

note.title: Describe with 有点
note.body: 有点 + adjective means “a little,” often for something unwelcome: 有点冷 means “a little cold.” 会 can express a future possibility: 下午会下雨 means “It will rain this afternoon.” The weather here is part of the practice dialogue.

title: Make weekend plans
description: Invite a friend and agree on a place and time.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.english: Let’s go to the park together.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: Sure! What time shall we meet?

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.hanzi: 星期六上午十点，在公园门口见。
dialogue.pinyin: Xīngqīliù shàngwǔ shí diǎn, zài gōngyuán ménkǒu jiàn.
dialogue.english: Let’s meet at the park entrance at ten on Saturday morning.

note.title: Time, place, then action
note.body: A common order is time + 在 + place + action: 星期六上午十点，在公园门口见。 空 is pronounced kòng in 有空, “to have free time.” It is kōng when it means “empty,” as in 空杯子, “an empty cup.”

title: Try something on
description: Choose a color and ask for a different size.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu yǒu lánsè de ma?
dialogue.english: Does this item of clothing come in blue?

dialogue.speaker: Seller
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒu. Nín chuān duō dà hào?
dialogue.english: Yes. What size do you wear?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Zhōng hào. Wǒ kěyǐ shì yíxià ma?
dialogue.english: Medium. May I try it on?

dialogue.speaker: Seller
dialogue.hanzi: 当然可以。试衣间在那边。
dialogue.english: Of course. The fitting room is over there.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒudiǎn xiǎo. Yǒu dà yìdiǎn de ma?
dialogue.english: It’s a little small. Do you have a larger one?

dialogue.speaker: Seller
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒu, wǒ gěi nín ná dà hào.
dialogue.english: Yes, I’ll get you a large.

vocabulary.english: measure word for items of clothing

note.title: Soften an action with 一下
note.body: Verb + 一下 suggests trying or doing something briefly: 试一下 means “give it a try.” 大一点 means “a little bigger.” In 有大一点的吗, 的 stands in for the clothing, so you don’t need to repeat 衣服.

title: Check into a hotel
description: Check a reservation and ask about breakfast.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.pinyin: Nín hǎo, qǐngwèn nín yǒu yùdìng ma?
dialogue.english: Hello. Do you have a reservation?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.english: Yes. My name is Lin An.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.pinyin: Nín zhù liǎng wǎn, duì ma?
dialogue.english: You’re staying for two nights, correct?

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.pinyin: Duì. Qǐngwèn, zǎocān jǐ diǎn kāishǐ?
dialogue.english: Correct. What time does breakfast start?

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.pinyin: Zǎoshang qī diǎn, zài yī lóu.
dialogue.english: At seven in the morning, on the ground floor.

note.title: Use 您 for polite address
note.body: 您 (nín) is a polite form of 你, often used when addressing a customer or an older person. A stay of two nights is 两晚. For numbered floors, 一 keeps its first tone: 一楼 (yī lóu). In this dialogue, 一楼 is the ground-level floor.

title: Keep the conversation going
pinyin: Kěyǐ zài shuō yí biàn ma
description: Ask for repetition, check a word, and confirm the details.

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.english: Let’s meet at the library entrance.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.hanzi: 不好意思，可以再说一遍吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi, kěyǐ zài shuō yí biàn ma?
dialogue.english: Sorry, could you say that again?

dialogue.speaker: Mei
dialogue.hanzi: 就是可以看书、借书的地方。
dialogue.pinyin: Jiù shì kěyǐ kàn shū, jiè shū de dìfang.
dialogue.english: It’s a place where you can read and borrow books.

dialogue.speaker: An
dialogue.hanzi: 明白了。我们两点见，对吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Míngbai le. Wǒmen liǎng diǎn jiàn, duì ma?
dialogue.english: Got it. We’re meeting at two, right?

vocabulary.english: one time all the way through

note.title: Three ways to get unstuck
note.body: Use 可以再说一遍吗？ to ask for repetition. Ask X 是什么意思？ to check what a word means. Add 对吗？ after what you heard to confirm it: 我们两点见，对吗？ These patterns help you keep practising in Mandarin.
